sources.title: Gnecchi-Ruscone and colleagues: Network of large pedigrees reveals social practices of Avar communities (2024)
sources.note: Abstract, Main, Marriage strategies, Community links and Conclusions; 424 individuals from four cemeteries. Biological relationships are not a complete account of social families.

sources.title: Nature: Ancient DNA reveals reproductive barrier despite shared Avar-period culture (2025)
sources.note: Abstract and Main: Leobersdorf and Modling, seventh- to eighth-century cemeteries, 722 individuals; shared culture did not imply identical ancestry or marriage networks.

sources.title: Metropolitan Museum: The Avar Treasure
sources.note: Vrap treasure ensemble, 600s-700s; uncertain attribution and ownership; Frankish campaigns in the 790s and early 800s.

sources.title: Metropolitan Museum: Medieval Art, A Resource for Educators
sources.note: Image 4, The Vrap Treasure, page 39: discovery in a copper cauldron in 1901, vessels and belt fittings; avoid its older categorical attribution in favor of current collection uncertainty.

sources.title: Metropolitan Museum: Ewer of Zenobius, 17.190.1704
sources.note: Object description: 700s silver-gilt ewer; Greek inscription; five engraved imitation control stamps rather than struck stamps.

sources.title: Marcel Erdal: Comments on N4183, Unicode working document N4197 (2012)
sources.note: Pages 2-3, discussion of Szarvas-Nagyszentmiklos and other Avar-period inscriptions; sound values and language remain undeciphered. A scholarly objection, not a Unicode endorsement of any decipherment.

sources.title: Johannes Preiser-Kapeller: The Climate of the Khagan (2018)
sources.note: Research abstract: environmental, written and archaeological evidence indicates growth in settlement and agricultural activity up to the middle eighth century; climate causation remains interpretive.

sources.title: Dan Shapira: Khazars, Encyclopaedia Iranica
sources.note: Origins, Khazar economy, The fall of Khazaria and Hebrew sources; seventh-century formation, diverse population, debated 960s collapse chronology and later manuscript copies.

sources.title: Fordham Medieval Sourcebook: Letters of Hasdai and King Joseph
sources.note: Primary correspondence in translation, approximately 960, sections I and II; distinguish the letters from dated editorial introduction and legendary conversion narrative.

sources.title: British Museum: Room 41 large-print guide, Khazars horse equipment
sources.note: Page 243, Bielowodsk, Perm, 1878,0509.46-48: dated AD 800s-900s; decorated iron stirrups and silver-covered bridle-bit, possible grave context.

sources.title: Valery Flyorov: Defense Capacity of Khazar Steppe Fortresses (2021)
sources.note: Abstract and pages 384-417: Sarkel, Semikarakorsk and Tsimliansk Right-bank fortress; building materials, internal divisions, workshops and limits of defensive interpretation.

sources.title: Princeton Geniza Project: T-S Misc. 35.38, Schechter letter
sources.note: Cambridge University Library manuscript, copied letter attributed to a Khazar Jew; Schechter transcription and translation. Recto left line 7, בארץ קזריא; recto left 13-16, Serah; verso left 12-14, royal marriage.

sources.title: Torres Prieto and Outhwaite: A reassessment of the Kyivan letter (2026)
sources.note: Peer-reviewed article abstract: a possible Khazar connection does not establish the Kyivan letter as a Khazarian artifact; signatories and background substantially Slavic.

sources.title: Bulgarian Ministry of Foreign Affairs: History
sources.note: Medieval and modern chronology: Christianity under Boris, Byzantine conquest 1018, renewed Bulgarian rule 1180s, Ottoman conquest, 1878 restoration, 1885 union, 1908 independence, 1946 republic and 1989 transition. Avoid its inaccurate compressed alphabet chronology and disputed massacre totals.

sources.title: Bulgarian Council of Ministers: History
sources.note: Sections 893-927, 1018-1185 and 1185-1396; broad phases only, excluding the page's internally inconsistent 1019 ending and rounded prisoner count.

sources.title: UNESCO: Madara Rider
sources.note: Description and Outstanding Universal Value: early eighth-century relief, sacred site, inscriptions and rulers; no inference that the portrayed event is a literal historical lion hunt.

sources.title: Lyudmila Doncheva-Petkova: Ceramic vessels from the biritual necropoleis and their metal parallels (2021)
sources.note: Abstract: Balchik, Novi Pazar, Kyulevcha and Topola cemetery vessels; metal/glass/wood parallels; production in early/mid eighth century and four Topola kilns.

sources.title: Archaeological Museum Veliki Preslav: Exhibition hall
sources.note: Everyday Life; Preslavian Painted Ceramics; Post-Capital Period. Household vessels, imported pottery, agricultural tools, adornment and local workshops.

sources.title: National Archaeological Institute: Ceramic Icon of St Theodore, tenth century
sources.note: Exhibit of July 2022; Patleina monastery excavations 1909, square tiles, local workshops; saint identification Stratelates or Tyron remains uncertain.

sources.title: Matilde Casas Olea: Contextos y funciones de las inscripciones sepulcrales protobulgaras (2019)
sources.note: Article page 353, inscription 66 on limestone: Κανα συβιγι Ωμ|ουρταγ. Greek funerary text for Turdatzis; script and borrowed Bulgar title distinguished. PDF: https://revistaseug.ugr.es/index.php/florentia/article/download/15596/13375/43920

sources.title: British Library: Gospels of Tsar Ivan Alexander, Add MS 39627
sources.note: Catalogue, manuscript of 1355-1356; royal portrait ff.2v-3r; chapter headings in gold, liturgical directions red; word square f.273v; colophon ff.274-275.

sources.title: Object Biographies and Biographical Objects from Medieval Bulgaria (2025)
sources.note: Contributions to Bulgarian Archaeology XV, pages 31-33: elite feasts and gift-giving; Pliska gold ring and evidence of adjustment; avoid identifying its unnamed portrait as a particular ruler.

sources.title: UNESCO: Bolgar Historical and Archaeological Complex
sources.note: Description, Outstanding Universal Value and authenticity: Volga-Kama setting, Islam 922, medieval city and later Golden Horde layers; distinguish restored structures from excavated originals.

sources.title: ICOMOS: Bolgar evaluation (2014)
sources.note: Historical development: trade and leatherwork, twelfth-century move of capital to Bilyar, Mongol destruction in 1236 and revival under the Golden Horde.

sources.title: Republic of Tatarstan: History of trade and economic connections
sources.note: Medieval section: cities, Volga trade routes, al-Gharnati's iron-goods/fur exchange account and rulers' customs duties.

sources.title: Bolgar Museum-Reserve on ARTEFACT: Chess piece
sources.note: Museum object: elk-antler rook, 3.6 x 4 x 2 cm, broad twelfth-fourteenth-century dating. Use object description; do not repeat its overgeneralized account of modern chess rules.

sources.title: Bolgar Museum-Reserve on ARTEFACT: Inkwell lid
sources.note: Second half of thirteenth century, copper-alloy inkwell lid with copper and silver decoration and Arabic blessing; clearly post-conquest evidence.

sources.title: Tatarica Encyclopedia: Bathhouse, F. F. Gulova
sources.note: First section only: five fourteenth-century Bolgar public baths; Red Chamber plan, underfloor heating and ceramic pipes. Later rural customs must not be projected into medieval Bulgaria.

sources.title: Bolgar Museum-Reserve on ARTEFACT: Tombstone, 1317
sources.note: Dated limestone epitaph, goldsmith Shahidullah; Arabic-script Tatar text in translation remembers respect for scholars and care for widows and orphans. Later Golden Horde context.

sources.title: National Library of Tatarstan: Medicine through the ages (2024)
sources.note: Exhibition introduction: adoption of Islam and Arabic literacy opened access to eastern medical works; a history of learning, not proof of efficacy of traditional treatments.

sources.title: National Assembly of Bulgaria: Brief history
sources.note: Historical discussion of Tarnovo Constitution 1879, July 1991 constitution, and National Assembly building 1884-1886; do not reuse outdated current assembly counts.

sources.title: National Assembly: Constitution of the Republic of Bulgaria
sources.note: Article 1(1), Bulgarian original; adopted 12 July 1991, promulgated 13 July. Quotation is seven Bulgarian words.

sources.title: UNESCO: Bulgarian Chitalishte, decision 12.COM 11.e.2
sources.note: 2017 decision, description of first centres in 1856, community foundation, intergenerational teaching, school collaboration and non-governmental status.

sources.title: UNESCO: Cultural practices associated to the 1st of March
sources.note: Living tradition shared by Bulgaria, North Macedonia, Moldova and Romania; red/white threads, signs of spring, intergenerational teaching; no precise ancient origin asserted.

sources.title: Sofia municipal tourism: Central Mineral Baths building
sources.note: Building 1906-1913, architects Momchilov and Grunanger, majolica decoration; later home of regional history museum.

sources.title: LB Bulgaricum: History of industrial production
sources.note: Producer's institutional history: Grigorov's 1905 research; mechanized pasteurization at Serdica dairy in Sofia in 1960. Exclude speculative claims of ancient invention and health benefits.

sources.title: US Holocaust Memorial Museum: Bulgaria
sources.note: Persecution of Jews: anti-Jewish measures, deportations from occupied Macedonia, Thrace and Pirot in March 1943; protests and cancellation in core Bulgarian provinces did not end internal displacement or forced labor.

sources.title: European Union: Bulgaria country profile
sources.note: Verified September 2026: EU membership from 1 January 2007; parliamentary republic. Avoid changeable officials, population figures and unneeded currency statements.

sources.title: Nomos: Obolos 39, lot 922, probable Volga-Bulgar imitation dirham
sources.note: Catalog of a physical coin, 30 mm and 1.89 g; Arabic transcription cites Samanid Nasr II, whose reign was 914-943. Attribution to Volga-Bulgar manufacture is explicitly probable, and the uniface coin has no surviving mint or date.

proposedOverrides.name: Bulgar Khanate
proposedOverrides.summary: A map label spanning medieval Balkan Bulgaria, including the Byzantine interval and the restored Bulgarian kingdom.

batchIdentityNotes.decision: Shared phased card, not an assertion that all labels are identical polities.
observations: Bulgars snapshot 600 is northern Black Sea; 700 includes duplicate civ geometry with one label Goths; 800 and 900 are Balkan.
Bulgar Khanate snapshots 1000-1400 are Balkan, not Volga; 1100 polygon is in the Byzantine sovereignty interval.
unresolved: Imported polygons and the Goths label require a separate geometry/identity audit.
Do not publish 600-1400 as one sovereign lifespan. Preserve map_coverage and visible Byzantine phase.

batchIdentityNotes.decision: Separate cards; imported map coverage retained as coverage, not sovereignty.
observations: Avars includes 900-1000 geometry although khaganate ended around 800.
Khazars includes 1000-1100 geometry after central power collapsed in the 960s.
Volga Bulgars extends to 1279 after the 1236 conquest.
unresolved: Geometry unchanged; late-label conflicts remain explicit and need future geometry correction.

batchIdentityNotes.decision: Modern state card, separate from medieval and Volga records.
observations: Index 1878-null, region Europe, alias Republic of Bulgaria.

unresolved: Avar-period runiform inscriptions are not securely deciphered, so no invented translation is supplied.
